Abstract: 2022) are reported for the first time from Guinea or Liberia. The females of these species are described and illustrated for the first time. Images of adults and the genitalia of all new species are provided.
Author: Karisch, Timm
Title: Lecithoceridae (Lepidoptera: Gelechioidea) from Nimba Mts. bordering Liberia and Guinea, Part I: The subfamily Torodorinae, with descriptions of 15 new species

Abstract: OBJECTIVES: Patient-specific mini-metal implants may represent a treatment option for middle-aged patients with focal (osteo-)chondral lesions of the distal femur when biological repair has failed or when other individual risk factors make biological repair unlikely to succeed. Both single-implant approaches for one and dual-implant approaches for two separate lesions in the same knee were investigated. This study evaluates the clinical performance of these implants for one or two lesions in one knee. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study was conducted using prospectively collected data of consecutive patients treated with one or two implants (Episealer® Implant, Episurf, Stockholm, Sweden) with a mean follow-up of 38 months. The Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain, adverse events, and conversions to unicompartmental or total knee arthroplasty were assessed. RESULTS: Statistically significant improvements in all KOOS subscales and VAS pain score compared to the preoperative values were observed in both groups (one implant n = 45; two implants n = 48; all p < 0.001). KOOS Symptoms improved from 48.7 ± 17.9 to 74.3 ± 21.6 in the one-implant group and from 44.7 ± 15.0 to 66.0 ± 24.8 in the two-implant group. Similar improvements were observed across all remaining KOOS subscales. The comparison between the two groups revealed slightly better improvements for the one-implant group. Implant survival according to Kaplan-Meier analysis was 88.1% for the one-implant group (number at risk = 21) and 83.4% for the two-implant group (number at risk = 27) after 60 months. CONCLUSION: Patient-specific mini-metal implants may represent a viable treatment option for middle-aged patients when biological repair is not feasible. Within the limitations of this study, the findings suggest that this approach can be considered for patients with one as well as patients with two (osteo-)chondral lesions. An acceptable implant survival was observed, regardless of lesion count. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.
Author: Malte Leo Rüter
Title: Mid-term clinical outcomes of one and two patient-specific mini-implants for focal (osteo-)chondral lesions of the distal femur.

Abstract: Abstract Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.
Author: Atirojwanich, Inkarat
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals

Abstract: Abstract Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.
Author: Ding, Junjie
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity

Abstract: ABSTRACT Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal‐Oxide‐Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion‐symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac‐frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight‐binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier‐free value for Δ below the nearest‐neighbour hopping amplitude t , and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t . Momentum‐space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein‐tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω‐shaped and power‐splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s − 1 . Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high‐capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.
Author: Mulla, Samina
Subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
Title: Photonic Klein Tunnelling in Silicon Topological Materials for Terahertz 6G Interconnects

Abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.
Author: Adamczyk, Sylwia
Title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability

Abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.
Author: Zheng, Yuhang
Title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades

Abstract: Atypical B-cells (ABCs) are observed across infections, yet their ontogeny and differentiation remain unclear. Using high-dimensional flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptomics, V(D)J sequencing, and functional assays in samples from individuals with malaria and healthy donors, we identify markers of cellular origin while tracking ABC differentiation. Early ABCs express CD11c and arise predominantly from memory B-cells. Two intermediate states originate from germinal center-derived and marginal zone-like B-cells. Pseudotime and lineage analyses reveal trajectories marked by progressive loss of CD24 and CD27, which is recapitulated in vitro, defining bona fide differentiation programs. Differentiation culminates in late ABCs lacking CD24, CD27, and CD21, while expressing CD11c, T-bet, and NKG7 at high levels, exhibiting partial overlap with double-negative-2 B-cells. Early and intermediate stages show greater plasma-cell differentiation potential and cytokine production capacity, whereas later stages acquire transcriptomic signatures of antigen presentation and association with microbial particles, defining stage-dependent functions that reconcile conflicting ABC roles. Comparable ABC populations occur in healthy blood and tonsils, with tissue-associated class switching and CD86 expression consistent with recent T-cell interaction. This framework consolidates ABC definitions along a single differentiation axis and clarifies their cellular origins.
Author: Courey‐Ghaouzi, Alan‐Dine
Title: Expression patterns of CD24 and CD27 resolve the origins and gradual differentiation of CD11c+ atypical memory B-cells after malaria infection

Abstract: Abstract Effective transdermal drug delivery (TDD) demands both the ability to bypass the stratum corneum (ST) and the robustness to sustain delivery efficiency under real-life conditions. Despite advances in nanocarriers, microneedles, and electrostimulation, many TDDS strategies face limitations due to cytotoxicity, invasiveness, device dependence, and poor performance for large molecules in real-world conditions. In this study, we present a marine-inspired TDDS patch (PDA@SC) that integrates adhesion strategies from marine organisms to achieve stable skin attachment and atraumatic macromolecular delivery, even on dynamic skin surfaces. The suction-cup (SC) structure, inspired by octopus’ suckers, generates negative pressure upon preload-induced deformation, promoting temporary mechanical modulation for nanolevel control of the ST barrier and enhancing drug delivery without external power. Simultaneously, the mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating modifies hydrophobic surfaces into high surface energy interfaces capable of chemical bonding, thereby ensuring intimate adhesion and minimizing drug leakage. Experimental findings confirmed that the delivery of the high molecular weight compound was enhanced on deformed skin, showing a 600% improvement compared to conventional topical application. In addition, preliminary human evaluation demonstrated that PDA@SC effectively improved key dermatological parameters. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of PDA@SC as a platform that can drive technological progress in wearable therapeutics and cosmetics.
Author: Song, Minwoo
Title: Marine-Inspired Synergistic Adhesion Enables Highly Efficient and Atraumatic Macromolecular Transdermal Delivery on Dynamic Skin

Abstract: Global efforts to turn waste into useful fuels have accelerated due to the growing demand for clean and sustainable energy, with hydrogen emerging as a vital energy carrier. Metals and metal oxides have shown remarkable promise as catalysts and functional elements in a variety of Waste-to-Hydrogen (WtH) pathways among the materials studied. The functions and mechanisms of metals and metal oxides in the three main processes of hydrogen generation via thermal, biochemical, and electrochemical conversion are critically examined in this review. Metal oxides aid in cracking, reforming, and tar reduction in thermal pathways like pyrolysis and gasification, increasing hydrogen yields and lowering carbon emissions. Metal oxide additives enhance microbial activity and electron transfer efficiency, which promotes the production of biohydrogen in biochemical processes, especially anaerobic digestion and dark fermentation. Metal and metal oxide-based catalysts are essential for enhancing electrocatalytic activity, stability, and overall system efficiency in electrochemical systems, such as water electrolysis and microbial electrolysis cells. Recent developments in hybrid catalyst systems, process integration techniques, and nanostructured and doped metal oxides are also covered in this review. The three WtH approaches are compared, with important considerations like economic viability, scalability, environmental impact, and energy efficiency assessed. Additionally, the incorporation of WtH technologies with carbon capture and circular economy principles is explored. By addressing current challenges and identifying future research directions, this review underscores the transformative potential of metal/metal oxides in advancing sustainable hydrogen production from waste resources.
Author: P. Sri Bala Jeya Krishna Sri
Title: A broad review of metal/metal oxide based integrated thermal, biochemical and electrochemical systems for waste into hydrogen conversion

Abstract: ABSTRACT Selective CO 2 ‐to‐formate electroreduction requires oxygen‐deficient SnO x sites that stabilize O‐bound * OCHO intermediates while resisting cathodic over‐reduction. Here, we use a precursor‐level coordination competition strategy to construct an oxygen vacancy (O v )‐rich SnO x catalyst coupled with isolated Cu–N sites through controlled conversion of amino‐functionalized Cu/Sn metal‐organic frameworks. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2‐aminoterephthalic acid (H 2 BDC‐NH 2 ) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnO x domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand‐derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu‐SnO x /NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy‐related SnO x environments and predominantly isolated Cu–N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O‐bound * OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnO x . Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate‐related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO 2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu‐SnO x /NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm −2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. Half‐cell and full‐cell energy efficiencies (EE) of 65% and 54%, respectively, were achieved in the flow cell and membrane electrode assembly (MEA). This work provides a coordination‐competition strategy for durable high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction.
Author: Wang, Zhuo
Subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
Title: Coordination Competition Couples Oxygen Vacancy‐Rich SnO x With Isolated Cu–N Sites for CO 2 ‐to‐formate Electroreduction

Abstract: Abstract Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and metal halide hydrate. SSNMR unambiguously reveals both the tert-butylammonium cation and the 18-crown-6 macrocycle as independent rotators─a distinction often ambiguous in such systems. Crucially, by correlating SSNMR-derived dynamics of the crown ether with dielectric relaxation of the coordinated water molecule, we uncover their synchronized rotation across a wide temperature range, mediated by charge-assisted hydrogen bonding. These findings reveal a cooperative multirotor gyroscopic model featuring synchronous rotation of an integrated coaxial crown ether–water–ammonium trio-rotator, accompanied by correlated alkyl reorientation. This synergy validates the dielectric relaxation principle in a complex, multirotor crystalline environment where unambiguous peak assignment has been a longstanding challenge. This work establishes a generalizable methodology for dissecting complex, multicomponent dynamics in crystalline materials, directly bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopic dielectric response.
Author: Wang, Qing
Title: Synergy of Solid-State NMR and Dielectric Spectroscopy Reveals Synchronized Multi-Rotor Dynamics in Crystalline Supramolecular Gyroscopes

Abstract: Abstract Problematic Internet Use (PIU) negatively impacts psychological, social, academic, and occupational functioning and is associated with unhealthy behaviors such as poor diet, inactivity, and sleep problems. The post-pandemic period has intensified Internet overuse, especially among young men, who are more prone to risky health behaviors. This study aimed to assess the relationship between health behaviors, PIU, and serotonin and dopamine levels in young men. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 325 men aged 18–30 from the West Pomeranian region of Poland. PIU severity was measured using the Internet Use Test (IUT), and health behaviors were assessed using the Health-Related Behavior Inventory (HBI). Blood samples were analyzed for serotonin and dopamine levels using ELISA. Results: 17.7% of participants exhibited high or very high PIU. One-third led unhealthy lifestyles. Higher PIU correlated with lower health behavior scores. The overall HBI score was negatively associated with non-work Internet use during weekdays and weekends. In the low PIU group, healthy eating habits positively correlated with dopamine levels. The linear correlation analysis, after adjusting for age and BMI, revealed a correlation between IUT scores and overall HBI scores, HBI healthy eating habits, and HBI positive mental attitudes. Conclusions: Increased Internet use was linked to poorer health behaviors. These findings underscore the need for interventions aimed at reducing Internet time and promoting healthy behaviors among young men with PIU. Further research should explore neurobiological mechanisms behind these associations.
Author: Kożybska, Marta
Title: Problematic internet use is associated with poorer health behaviours and peripheral serotonin levels in young men

Abstract: This study examined how transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) interacts with high-intensity interval training (HIIT) to shape cardiopulmonary fitness and executive function in elite endurance athletes across an 8-week protocol. Sixty-six nationally ranked athletes were stratified by training tenure, competitive level, and baseline maximal oxygen uptake, then prospectively allocated, with participant and outcome-assessor blinding, to one of three intervention arms: real-tDCS plus HIIT, sham-tDCS plus HIIT, or HIIT-only; 59 completed the programme. Both stimulation arms alternated between a left dorsolateral prefrontal montage and a bilateral motor montage, and cortical target was carried through the analysis as a within-subject factor rather than folded into a single stimulation label. Cardiopulmonary indices, executive function (Stroop, N-back, Flanker), prefrontal hemodynamics via functional near-infrared spectroscopy, and heart rate variability were measured at four assessment waves, with female athletes tested inside the early follicular window at every wave. Nonlinear mixed-effects and generalized additive mixed models resolved dynamic trajectories at the individual level, while a second-order partial derivative quantified the stimulation × load interaction. End-of-study allocation guesses did not depart from chance in either masked arm, so blinding held. Because masking held only for the two stimulation arms, the real- versus sham-tDCS comparison carries the causal weight of the trial, and the HIIT-only arm enters as a partially unblinded reference rather than a second control. Against sham, the real-tDCS arm showed a delayed but steeper rise in maximal oxygen uptake and an earlier separation in Stroop interference. A modelled cumulative exposure-response surface exhibited a non-monotone shape with an interior maximum whose geometry, but not whose coordinates, survived leave-one-subject-out cross-validation; because intensity and duration were fixed and exposure varied only with session completion, we present that surface as exploratory. Cross-system coupling between prefrontal oxygenation and ventilatory threshold strengthened under active stimulation, consistent with, though not proof of, a bidirectional central-peripheral regulation account. Adherence captured the largest share of individual response variance, with BDNF and ACTN3 variants contributing modestly. As exploratory findings, these patterns are consistent with a stratified, trajectory-aware view of neuromodulation in elite training, though claims about an optimal dose must await confirmatory trials that deliberately vary stimulation intensity.
Author: Dai, Chunmin
Title: Trajectories of cardiopulmonary adaptation and executive function in elite endurance athletes receiving transcranial direct current stimulation with interval training

Abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) enables low-latency services by migrating computational resources closer to end-users. However, as mobile workloads increasingly adopt complex Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topologies, system performance is strongly affected by interdependent data shuffling across the inter-server fabric and synchronization constraints during uplink transmission. Existing models frequently neglect physical fabric capacity limits and decouple communication from computation, leading to inefficient energy usage and increased latency. In this paper, we propose a coupled Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) formulation that jointly optimizes multi-AP association, task placement, Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), and explicit inter-server routing under per-application deadline constraints. To address the inherent non-convexity and combinatorial complexity of the joint problem, we introduce the ECO-EDGE framework. ECO-EDGE decomposes the original MINLP using a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) architecture and solves relaxed subproblems via tailored convexification techniques, including McCormick-based convex envelopes for bilinear placement products, a “Bits-per-RB” formulation that maps communication constraints into exponential cones, and power- and rotated second-order cone representations for computation and fabric delay modeling. The resulting relaxed BCD scheme exhibits monotonic objective decrease under exact block solution, while deterministic rounding and topological list-scheduling are applied to recover feasible schedules, which are subsequently verified for deadline satisfaction. Simulation results in dense multi-AP deployments show that ECO-EDGE reduces total system energy by up to \(81.8\%\) compared to a Local-Only baseline and achieves an empirical deadline satisfaction rate of \(97.9\%\) , outperforming heuristic, fabric-oblivious, and disjoint optimization baselines.
Author: Alymani, Mofadal
Title: ECO-EDGE: joint DAG offloading and fabric routing in Multi-AP MEC via conic optimization

Abstract: Guided by Belsky’s parenting process model, this pooled cross-sectional study examined a theory-ordered pattern of statistical associations linking marital satisfaction, mindful parenting, parental involvement, and parent-reported emotional competence. Participants were 5,303 married biological parents of kindergarten children in Hubei Province, China, most of whom were mothers. A latent-variable structural equation model adjusted for data-collection batch and relevant demographic characteristics; classroom-cluster-robust re-estimation was used to evaluate the nested recruitment structure. Marital satisfaction was positively associated with mindful parenting and parental involvement; mindful parenting and parental involvement were each positively associated with parent-reported emotional competence. The theory-ordered statistical indirect association through the serially specified parenting constructs was positive (β = 0.038, cluster-robust 95% CI [0.029, 0.046]), whereas the adjusted direct association between marital satisfaction and parent-reported emotional competence was nonsignificant. Covariance-equivalent directional specifications fit identically, indicating that temporal and causal ordering could not be established. Because all constructs were reported by the same parent at one time point, the findings describe theory-consistent statistical associations and do not show that one parenting process preceded another, transmitted an effect, or would improve the child outcome if changed. Longitudinal and multi-informant research is needed.
Author: Wang, Tongyao
Title: Marital satisfaction and parent-reported emotional competence in Chinese preschoolers: serial indirect associations through mindful parenting and parental involvement
Topic: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

Abstract: Abstract Aging is a complex biological process influenced by chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation, collectively termed inflammaging. The HEBE (Healthy aging versus inflamm-aging: the role of physical Exercise in modulating the Biomarkers of age-associated and Environmentally determined chronic diseases) project developed and implemented a consortium-driven, cost-effective methodological framework for biomarker profiling aimed at capturing these mechanisms and their modulation by lifestyle interventions, particularly physical exercise. This framework integrates interdisciplinary expertise and high-throughput analytical strategies to guide biomarker selection while balancing physiological relevance, analytical feasibility, and cost-effectiveness. The framework was applied within a large multidisciplinary consortium structured across multiple research lines (RLs), each addressing specific domains of inflammaging-related conditions, including obesity, cancer, frailty, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, neuroinflammation, psychological stress, autoimmune disorders, and fertility. The resulting biomarker panel spans molecular, cellular, and systemic levels, encompassing inflammatory cytokines, metabolic regulators, neurotrophic factors, extracellular vesicle-derived molecules, lipidomics, proteomics, and platelet activation markers. A key output of this framework is the harmonized integration of cross-disciplinary biomarker data while minimizing biological sample consumption and analytical costs. The prioritization of multiplex technologies and targeted omics approaches enables the simultaneous assessment of multiple biomarkers from limited biospecimens, enhancing efficiency and scalability. Centralized data management and statistical coordination further support consistency of implementation. This work also highlights methodological challenges inherent to large-scale biomarker studies, including inter-individual variability, platform standardization, and the need for longitudinal validation. Addressing these issues through harmonized protocols and extended follow-up will be essential to strengthen future empirical applications. By formalizing and documenting this consortium-driven approach, the HEBE Project provides a transferable methodological framework to support biomarker-based monitoring of aging processes and lifestyle interventions in complex, resource-constrained research settings.
Author: Bollati, Valentina
Title: A consortium-driven framework for biomarker prioritization in the HEBE aging study

Abstract: Greenhouse operators face high pesticide exposure risks, yet the cognitive pathways translating health literacy (HL) into preventive behaviors remain unclear. This study examined the multidimensional construct of Pesticide Health Literacy (PHL) and its association with preventive behaviors among greenhouse operators. This cross-sectional census study was conducted among 115 greenhouse operators in Neyshabur County, Iran. Data were collected using validated PHL and preventive behavior questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and hierarchical multiple regression. Participants exhibited moderate PHL (mean: 61.92 ± 16.96 out of 115) but significantly lower preventive behaviors (mean: 8.90 ± 1.74 out of 21). Hierarchical multiple regression revealed that PHL was the strongest independent factor associated with preventive behaviors ( β = 0.63, P < 0.001 ), followed by educational attainment ( β = 0.37, P < 0.001 ). Sociodemographic variables alone did not significantly explain variation in preventive behaviors (R 2 = 0.084 , P = 0.140 ). PHL, particularly the critical information assessment domain, showed a stronger association with preventive behaviors than the sociodemographic factors examined in this study. The findings suggest that interventions addressing pesticide safety should extend beyond basic information provision and include skills for critically evaluating pesticide-related information, particularly among operators with lower educational attainment. Such an approach may help address the gap in HL preventive behaviors in high-risk agricultural settings.
Author: Ali Akbar Mahmoodı
Title: Pesticide health literacy and preventive behaviors among greenhouse operators in Northeastern Iran

Abstract: Abstract Freshwater chelonians face severe extinction risk, and head-starting programs increasingly rely on captive rearing to offset poor recruitment. However, evaluating success by growth and release numbers overlooks welfare and post-release competence. We assessed head-started Critically Endangered Batagur dhongoka and Batagur kachuga under five enrichment treatments, combining growth data with individual-level behavioural scans and 24-hour group activity budgets over 367 days. Final body mass was highest under mixed enrichment (141.1 g) and lowest under no-enrichment (108.1 g). B. kachuga were heavier than B. dhongoka under all treatments. Enrichment-related behaviour was highest under natural enrichment (52.5%) and lowest under no-enrichment (11.9%), while stress-related behaviour was lowest under seminatural enrichment (1.6%) and highest under no-enrichment (10.7%). Mixed enrichment produced the highest basking response and most balanced group activity budget; natural enrichment the highest shelter-use response. Integrating growth and behaviour at the same month × species × treatment scale, natural enrichment ranked first, mixed second, and no-enrichment last. Environmental enrichment shapes growth and behaviour differently; growth and behavioural metrics should therefore be treated as complementary rather than interchangeable indicators of captive-rearing success. Each species-treatment combination comprised a single chamber, with individual-level behaviour from one marked animal; results are therefore descriptive rather than independently replicated.
Author: Ashish Kumar Panda
Title: Environmental enrichment affects growth and behaviour differently in head-started critically endangered freshwater turtles

Abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is a key regulator of vascular homeostasis and host–microbe interactions. In addition to the endogenous nitric oxide synthase (NOS) pathway, the enterosalivary nitrate–nitrite–NO pathway provides an alternative source of NO and critically depends on oral nitrate-reducing bacteria (ONRB). This review examines the oral microbiome–NO axis and its role in nitrate metabolism, NO homeostasis, and oral–systemic interactions. A narrative review integrating microbiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence on oral nitrate metabolism, ONRB activity, and their impact on oral and systemic outcomes, including dietary and antiseptic interventions. The functional activity and nitrate-reducing capacity of the oral microbiome are key determinants of nitrate reduction and systemic NO bioavailability. Oral dysbiosis, periodontal disease, and antiseptic mouthwash use impair ONRB activity and nitrite production, potentially affecting vascular function and blood pressure. Conversely, dietary nitrate enhances ONRB activity and nitrate-to-nitrite conversion, supporting oral and vascular health. Interindividual variability, partly influenced by sex-related factors, may contribute to heterogeneous responses. The oral microbiome–NO axis represents a functional interface between host physiology and microbial metabolism, linking oral ecology with vascular regulation. Through their activity, ONRB contribute to NO homeostasis, highlighting nitrate bioactivation as an important component of host–microbe interactions with implications for oral and systemic physiology. Recognition of this pathway expands current understanding of host–microbe cooperation in NO homeostasis and may inform future microbiome-based approaches to support oral and cardiovascular health.
Author: Altamura, Serena
Title: Oral Nitrate-Reducing Bacteria and Nitric Oxide Homeostasis: Functional Host–Microbe Interactions in Oral and Vascular Health

Abstract: Pigmented red rice is a promising functional whole grain, but conventional milling cannot fully release its intracellular bioactives due to dense bran cell walls. Superfine grinding can effectively destroy compact tissue structures and improve the processing characteristics of cereal powders. In this study, red rice powders (RRPs) with different particle sizes were prepared by superfine grinding, and their physicochemical properties, micromorphology, crystalline structure, total phenolic content (TPC), pasting behaviors, and in vitro starch digestibility were tested by particle size analysis, colorimetric measurement, SEM, XRD, FT-IR, the Folin–Ciocalteu method, RVA, and an in vitro simulated digestion model. The results show that superfine grinding caused severe matrix destruction, reducing the particle size (D90) by 83.5%, and remarkably increasing the specific surface area. Furthermore, superfine grinding improved color brightness, decreased powder flowability, and reduced starch crystallinity, while no new functional groups were generated. Additionally, the TPC and water/oil-holding capacity were effectively enhanced. The pasting properties and in vitro starch digestibility of RRP were modified by superfine grinding. This study provides basic data on RRP properties and recommends the selection of proper grinding intensity in order to obtain powder for diverse food applications, such as functional beverages and bakery products.
Author: 郭晓娟
Title: Effects of Superfine Grinding on Physicochemical Properties and In Vitro Starch Digestibility of Red Rice Powder

Abstract: BACKGROUND: Meta-analyses require the calculation of effect sizes for all included studies. The most common experimental design in exercise intervention studies is the pre-post control design. A number of different approaches exist for calculating effect sizes for this design, and it is currently unknown which calculation methods are actually used in the published exercise science literature and how this might impact results. METHODS: We extracted all meta-analyses (N = 101) published in six journals over a 2-year period where the primary studies used a pre-post control design. We recalculated randomly selected primary study effect sizes in each meta-analysis to determine the calculation methods used and compare them to the reported methods. An example case was used to illustrate the impact of using different calculation methods on meta-analysis outcomes. RESULTS: We identified a total of 50 unique combinations of calculation methods among the n = 91 meta-analyses for which we could determine the calculation procedure. Most researchers used change score-based standardized mean differences. These required the imputation of a pre-post correlation, for which most authors used fixed benchmarks instead of evidence-based or previously reported values. Reporting was often incomplete and we identified major issues in the calculation of at least 27 articles. We demonstrate that different calculation methods can yield different meta-analysis outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Effect size calculation procedures vary widely, which can affect meta-analysis outcomes and mislead their interpretation. A considerable number of published meta-analytical findings in exercise science may differ when other reasonable or corrected calculation methods are used. We provide recommendations on how to choose an appropriate effect size method for the pre-post control design. We encourage researchers to transparently report and justify the procedures used and perform sensitivity analyses when performing meta-analyses.
Author: Nolte, Simon
Title: Effect Size Calculation Procedures in Exercise Intervention Meta-Analyses: A Scoping Review

Abstract: ABSTRACT How do investor reactions to the mandatory disclosure of firm tax information influence managers' reporting choices? To answer this question, we build a structural model of reporting bias, which we test with a unique data set of Turkish firms that have been mandated to publicly disclose their tax returns since 2009. We find that both book and tax income numbers are informative to investors. Structural estimates are consistent with disclosure of the tax report reducing both market incentives to manage book earnings and investor uncertainty about underlying firm value. Tax disclosure is associated with higher reported tax income, though the increase is not statistically significant. Counterfactual estimates suggest that book‐tax‐conformity could change financial and tax reporting biases, but lead to a lower quality information environment relative to the separate disclosure of book and tax reports.
Author: Eric J. Allen
Title: The effect of the mandatory disclosure of corporate tax returns on reporting bias

Abstract: Digital trade drives global trade expansion, yet its environmental implications remain ambiguous. This paper examines whether digital trade rules in regional trade agreements reduce bilateral trade-embodied carbon emissions, through which channels, and under what conditions. Using a rule depth index from TAPED matched with Eora bilateral embodied carbon, we estimate a high-dimensional fixed-effects model on a bilateral country–pair–year panel covering 188 economies over 2000–2023, with an instrumental variable based on lagged digital governance network size. Deeper rules significantly reduce embodied carbon. The composition and technique effects lower emissions, with the technique effect dominant; the scale channel’s indirect effect is not significant. The reduction is stronger for Global North pairs and highly binding provisions; pioneer exporters gain less, agreement upgrading does not significantly strengthen it, and the reduction varies by rule template. Carbon pricing attenuates the reduction, indicating partial substitution with environmental regulation. An event study, an extensive/intensive margin decomposition, and carbon leakage checks corroborate these findings. Rules advance climate objectives only if environmental provisions enter institutional design from the outset and are backed by domestic regulation. The index captures rule depth through provision coverage and binding force but cannot fully capture implementation quality.
Author: Zhou, Ying
Title: Digital Trade Rules and Embodied Carbon Emissions: A Scale–Composition–Technique Analysis

Abstract: Abstract In this paper we review some analytic results on the dynamics of the FPU system. In the first part of the paper, having in mind that the FPU Hamiltonian and the Toda Hamiltonian are close to each other, we present some results on the action angle variables of the Toda system and deduce some stability properties for the dynamics of the FPU system. We first focus on the case of finitely many particles and then we study the limit $$N\rightarrow \infty $$ N → ∞ . We also present some results on the continuous limit of the Toda chain showing that it is well described by a couple of KdV equations. Then we study directly the dynamics of the function interpolating the FPU system and show that the dynamics is Hamiltonian and that the Hamiltonian is very close to a function of the first three Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy. In the second part of the paper we present some results valid in the thermodynamic limit, according to which the time auto correlation functions of some suitably constructed observables decay slowly implying lower bounds on the thermalization times of the system.
Author: Bambusi, Dario
Title: A Survey on Rigorous Results for the Dynamics of Periodic FPU Chains

Abstract: In Religion for Realists , sociologist Samuel L. Perry addresses a critical empirical puzzle that also reveals a central weakness in the social scientific study of religion: why do scholars, journalists, and the general public consistently misinterpret religious behavior and macro-level shifts in religion?He identifies the root of this widespread misunderstanding as the intellectual dominance of Anglo-Protestant misconceptions about religion.This paradigm equates religion almost exclusively with individual theological belief, rational choice, and personal piety, obscuring the mechanisms that drive religious and political behavior in contemporary society.
Author: Hou, Zikang
Source: Journal for the Scientific Study of Religion
Title: Religion for Realists: Why We All Need the Scientific Study of Religion
